findings.title: Hardcoded AWS access key committed to the repository
findings.evidence: A module-level constant holds what is clearly an AWS access key id: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "[REDACTED-AWS-KEY]"'. Any principal with read access to this repo (or to build artifacts, CI logs that echo the file, or a cloned fork) obtains a long-lived credential; nothing in the diff restricts its permissions or rotates it.
findings.recommendation: Remove the constant entirely. Load credentials from the ambient provider chain (env vars AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, ~/.aws/credentials, or an IAM role) and rely on boto3's default resolution; if an explicit source is required, read it with os.environ[...] and fail loudly when absent. Rotate/revoke the exposed key in IAM, and purge it from history (the commit remains in git history even after deletion). Add a secret scanner (e.g. detect-secrets/gitleaks) to CI to prevent recurrence.

findings.title: Secret constant is defined but never used by the boto3 client
findings.evidence: The next line constructs the client as 'client = boto3.client("s3", region_name=REGION)' with no aws_access_key_id argument, so the newly added constant is dead code: it leaks the credential without affecting which credentials the client actually uses. If the intent was to make the deploy use this key, the change silently does not do that.
findings.recommendation: Delete the constant rather than wiring it in. If explicit credentials really are needed, pass them via the standard chain (env vars or a named profile with boto3.Session) instead of inlining them, and add a test/assertion that the module contains no literal credential material.
